parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Carboplatin and satraplatin are used as anticancer drugs instead of cisplatin.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Describe the action of cisplatin as an anticancer drug.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the geometry of the platinum centre in the carboplatin complex.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why carboplatin does **not** show cis-trans isomerism.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Satraplatin is a neutral complex, containing the ligands $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^-$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NH}_2$, $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{NH}_3$.

Deduce the oxidation state of platinum in satraplatin.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Compound $\mathbf{M}$ is made from 1,3-dimethylbenzene in a two-step synthesis.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest reactants and conditions for each step of this synthesis.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
A student investigates a possible synthesis of $\mathbf{M}$ directly from benzene using $\text{COCl}_2$ in the presence of an $\text{AlCl}_3$ catalyst.

Benzene initially reacts with $\text{COCl}_2$ as shown.

**reaction 1** $\text{COCl}_2 + \text{AlCl}_3 \rightarrow \text{AlCl}_4^- + \text{Cl}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}$

**reaction 2** $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} + \text{H}^+$

Reaction 2 is the electrophilic substitution of $\text{Cl}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}=\text{O}$ for $\text{H}^+$ in benzene.

Suggest a mechanism for reaction 2.
